title: Freelance Motion Designer
intro: Our interfaces aren’t static—they’re living, breathing systems. Every transition, hover, and microinteraction matters. This role exists to bring that life into our products—to make motion feel purposeful, responsive, and human.
workOn: Crafting microinteractions and motion systems that make our interfaces feel alive and responsive
Collaborating with designers and engineers to define how products move, react, and communicate
Prototyping motion concepts that enhance clarity, feedback, and emotion
Pushing the edge of how AI and robotics interfaces feel—not just how they look
bring: A strong sense for motion as communication—not decoration
Experience creating microinteractions, transitions, and motion systems for digital products
Ability to prototype ideas quickly in tools like After Effects, Principle, or Figma
An eye for rhythm, timing, and flow—knowing when to add energy and when to hold still
Collaboration skills to work closely with designers, engineers, and clients
Curiosity about robotics, AI, and how motion can make technology feel more human
niceToHave: Experience animating logos, icons, or visual identities
Familiarity with motion for brand storytelling and product launches
Comfort working with 3D or physics-based motion tools
Curiosity about how motion can make interfaces breathe, signal, and feel alive
howWeWork: Weekly “Design Together” sessions with clients—zero waiting weeks for feedback.
Twice-weekly Slack updates keep pulses steady.
Small senior team, flat hierarchy, big ownership.
We meet once a year in different parts of the world to connect, plan, and reset.
applySteps: One project you’re proud of & why (tweet length)
